slices.label: The Fourth Crusade shatters Byzantium
events: Crusaders sack Constantinople; Latin Empire founded, Greek rump states flee to Nicaea, Epirus, Trebizond
Philip II Augustus conquers Normandy and Anjou from King John of England
Kaloyan's Bulgaria dominant in the Balkans after Byzantine collapse
slices.connectivityNote: Champagne fairs and Italian galleys knit the west together even as the Fourth Crusade wrecks the Levant trade's eastern anchor.

entities.name: Kingdom of England
entities.note: John Lackland just lost Normandy & Anjou to France; Aquitaine and Ireland held.

entities.name: Welsh Principalities
entities.note: Gwynedd under Llywelyn the Great rising over rival Welsh princes and Marcher lords.

entities.name: Gaelic Irish Kingdoms
entities.note: Gaelic Ulster kingdoms resisting Anglo-Norman advance.

entities.name: Kingdom of Castile
entities.note: Fresh from Las Navas de Tolosa's build-up; dominant Christian Iberian power.

entities.name: Crown of Aragon
entities.note: Peter II rules Aragon-Catalonia plus Provence.

entities.name: Almohad Caliphate
entities.note: Berber caliphate spanning Maghreb and al-Andalus; cracks widening before Las Navas (1212).

entities.name: County of Toulouse
entities.note: Rich Occitan county, soon target of the Albigensian Crusade (1209).

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Philip II Augustus doubles the royal domain by seizing Normandy (1204).

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Philip of Swabia vs Otto IV civil war over the imperial throne.

entities.name: County of Flanders
entities.note: Count Baldwin IX just crowned Latin Emperor at Constantinople.

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: Innocent III at the height of papal authority.

entities.name: Hohenstaufen Kingdom of Sicily
entities.note: Wealthiest Mediterranean kingdom; young Frederick II a royal ward.

entities.name: Baltic Tribes
entities.note: Livonian Crusade just beginning (Riga founded 1201).

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland
entities.note: Fragmented among rival Piast duchies since 1138.

entities.name: Rus Principalities
entities.note: Rurikid principalities feuding; Kyiv's primacy fading toward Vladimir-Suzdal.

entities.name: Cuman-Kipchak Confederation
entities.note: Turkic nomad confederation dominates the Pontic-Caspian steppe.

entities.name: Banate of Bosnia
entities.note: Ban Kulin's realm accused of Bogomil heresy by Rome.

entities.name: Republic of Venice
entities.note: Chief architect and beneficiary of the Fourth Crusade; seizes Crete and Aegean/Adriatic ports.

entities.name: Kingdom of Serbia
entities.note: Grand Principality of the Nemanjić dynasty.

entities.name: Latin Empire
entities.note: Baldwin I's crusader state carves up the Byzantine core.

entities.name: Despotate of Epirus
entities.note: Michael I Komnenos Doukas founds a Greek successor state in the west.

entities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire
entities.note: Kaloyan exploits Byzantium's collapse, expanding into Thrace and Macedonia.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: Theodore Laskaris organizes Greek resistance from Nicaea after the sack of Constantinople.

entities.name: Empire of Trebizond
entities.note: Alexios I Komnenos founds this Pontic Greek splinter state weeks before the Latin conquest.

entities.name: Kingdom of Cilician Armenia
entities.note: Leo I crowned king in 1198 with Papal blessing.

entities.name: Kingdom of Georgia
entities.note: Queen Tamar's golden age; Georgian-Armenian power projects into Anatolia.

entities.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
entities.note: Egypt, Syria and the Jazira under Saladin's heirs.

entities.name: Kingdom of Jerusalem (Acre)
entities.note: Kingdom of Jerusalem reduced to a coastal strip after Hattin (1187); capital now Acre.

entities.name: Abbasid Caliphate
entities.note: Caliph al-Nasir rebuilding some temporal authority in Iraq.

relations.note: Nicaean Greeks resist the Latin conquest
Kaloyan presses the fledgling Latin Empire's borders
Venice's commercial empire underwrites the Latin conquest
Philip II strips John of Normandy and Anjou
Iberian frontier tense ahead of Las Navas de Tolosa (1212)
Georgian-Seljuk contest for eastern Anatolia
Greek successor states resist Frankish partition

slices.label: Klokotnitsa and the union of León-Castile
events: John Asen II crushes Epirus at Klokotnitsa; Bulgaria dominates the Balkans from Belgrade to the Aegean
Ferdinand III permanently unites León and Castile
Teutonic Knights invited into Prussia; James I of Aragon conquers Mallorca (1229)
slices.connectivityNote: Commercial revolution in full swing: Champagne fairs, Italian communes, and a Mediterranean reopening to Genoese and Venetian galleys.

entities.name: Kingdom of England
entities.note: Henry III's minority ends; Earldom of Ulster (1205) extends royal reach into Ireland.

entities.name: Welsh Principalities
entities.note: Llywelyn the Great dominates Gwynedd and much of native Wales.

entities.name: Kingdom of Castile
entities.note: Ferdinand III's 1230 union of León and Castile creates Iberia's dominant Christian power.

entities.name: Crown of Aragon
entities.note: James I 'the Conqueror' takes Mallorca (1229); Valencia campaign brewing.

entities.name: Taifa al-Andalus (Ibn Hud)
entities.note: Post-Almohad Taifa chaos under Ibn Hud; Castile and Aragon pressing hard.

entities.name: Almohad Caliphate
entities.note: Maghreb heartland still held, but Iberian authority has evaporated since Las Navas (1212).

entities.name: County of Toulouse
entities.note: Devastated by the Albigensian Crusade; Treaty of Paris (1229) leaves Raymond VII a reduced vassal county.

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Louis IX (Saint Louis) succeeds; royal domain consolidated after Normandy and Anjou's conquest.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Frederick II, also King of Sicily, rules in absentia; princes gain ground (Statutum in favorem principum, 1232).

entities.name: County of Flanders
entities.note: Cloth towns Ghent, Bruges and Ypres booming.

entities.name: Hohenstaufen Kingdom of Sicily
entities.note: Frederick II's 'Stupor Mundi' court at Palermo; also Holy Roman Emperor since 1220.

entities.name: Republic of Pisa
entities.note: Rivalry with Genoa sharpening over Sardinia and Corsica.

entities.name: Finnic Tribes
entities.note: Swedish crusading pressure building ahead of the 1249 conquest of Tavastia.

entities.name: Teutonic Order
entities.note: Invited into Prussia by Duke Konrad of Masovia (1226); Livonian crusade (Riga 1201) largely complete.

entities.name: Baltic Tribes
entities.note: Lithuanian tribes not yet unified; Mindaugas's rise still a few years off.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland
entities.note: Still fragmented among rival Piast duchies.

entities.name: Rus Principalities
entities.note: Vladimir-Suzdal ascendant under Yuri II; Galicia-Volhynia consolidating under Daniel Romanovich.

entities.name: Cuman-Kipchak Confederation
entities.note: Mongol pressure looms from the east after Jebe and Subutai's 1223 raid (Kalka River).

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
entities.note: Andrew II and Béla IV; Golden Bull (1222) checks royal power.

entities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire
entities.note: John Asen II's empire at its medieval zenith after Klokotnitsa (1230): Belgrade to the Aegean.

entities.name: Latin Empire
entities.note: Reduced to Constantinople and its immediate hinterland, squeezed by Bulgaria and Nicaea.

entities.name: Despotate of Epirus
entities.note: Theodore Komnenos Doukas captured at Klokotnitsa; realm shattered.

entities.name: Principality of Achaea
entities.note: Villehardouin principality at its Frankish chivalric height.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: John III Vatatzes builds Nicaea into the strongest Greek successor state.

entities.name: Sultanate of Rum
entities.note: Alaeddin Kayqubad I's golden age; caravanserais and Konya's Seljuk architecture flourish.

entities.name: Kingdom of Georgia
entities.note: Queen Rusudan reigns; first Mongol raid (1221-22) a grim omen.

entities.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
entities.note: Al-Kamil cedes Jerusalem to Frederick II by treaty (1229) rather than by the sword.

entities.name: Kingdom of Jerusalem (Acre)
entities.note: Jerusalem restored to Christian rule by the Sixth Crusade's diplomacy (1229-1244).

entities.name: Hafsid Ifriqiya
entities.note: Abu Zakariya breaks from Almohad rule (1229), founding independent Ifriqiya from Tunis.

relations.note: Klokotnitsa (1230) shatters Epirote power
Bulgaria squeezes the Latin Empire toward Constantinople alone
Ferdinand III's union with León accelerates the Reconquista
James I conquers Mallorca (1229), eyes Valencia next
Hafsids break away from a crumbling Almohad Caliphate
Crusading conquest of Prussia begins in earnest
Rival maritime republics both profit from the reopened eastern Mediterranean

slices.label: The Mongol storm breaks over Eastern Europe
events: Mongols annihilate a Polish-German army at Legnica and the Hungarian royal army at Mohi in the same month
Kyiv lies in ruins (sacked December 1240); the Rus principalities and steppe fall under Mongol rule
Hungary devastated and occupied; Béla IV a fugitive on the Dalmatian coast
slices.connectivityNote: The Mongol conquest severs the Rus river trade and empties whole regions even as it plants the seeds of the future Pax Mongolica.

entities.name: Kingdom of England
entities.note: Henry III's long personal rule; baronial tensions building.

entities.name: Kingdom of Castile
entities.note: Fresh conquest of Córdoba (1236); Seville campaign underway.

entities.name: Crown of Aragon
entities.note: James I completes the conquest of Valencia (1238).

entities.name: Emirate of Granada
entities.note: Muhammad I ibn Nasr founds the Nasrid emirate (1238) as a Castilian tributary, the last independent Muslim Iberian state.

entities.name: Almohad Caliphate
entities.note: Confined now to the Maghreb heartland; Marinid tribesmen encroach from the east.

entities.name: Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen
entities.note: Yaghmurasen founds the Zayyanid kingdom at Tlemcen (1236) as Almohad power fails.

entities.name: County of Toulouse
entities.note: Raymond VII's reduced county, hemmed in by French royal officials.

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Louis IX's France is Europe's wealthiest and most orderly kingdom.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Frederick II excommunicated (1239), locked in total war with the Papacy.

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: At open war with Emperor Frederick II.

entities.name: Hohenstaufen Kingdom of Sicily
entities.note: Frederick II's kingdom bears the brunt of the imperial-papal war.

entities.name: Novgorod Republic
entities.note: Alexander (soon Nevsky) defeats a Swedish force at the Neva (1240); Mongols spare the city but exact tribute.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
entities.note: Mindaugas begins uniting the Lithuanian tribes against Rus and crusader pressure alike.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland
entities.note: Duke Henry II of Silesia dies at Legnica; the Mongols withdraw westward after the battle, sparing the kingdom's core.

entities.name: Rus Principalities
entities.note: Polotsk, in the marshy northwest, escapes the Mongol storm that consumes the rest of Rus.

entities.name: Mongol Empire
entities.note: Batu Khan's western campaign: Vladimir, Chernigov, Kyiv sacked; Hungary occupied; Poland raided at Legnica.

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
entities.note: Royal army destroyed at Mohi; King Béla IV a fugitive in Dalmatia while Mongols occupy the plain.

entities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire
entities.note: John Asen II dies in 1241; succession crisis looms just as the Mongol wave passes to the north.

entities.name: Latin Empire
entities.note: Baldwin II rules little beyond Constantinople's walls.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: Nicaea untouched by the Mongols, quietly building the strength that will retake Constantinople.

entities.name: Sultanate of Rum
entities.note: Mongol vanguards probing the eastern frontier; catastrophe at Köse Dağ only two years away.

entities.name: Kingdom of Georgia
entities.note: Formally submits to the Mongols under Queen Rusudan (1243 treaty being negotiated).

entities.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
entities.note: As-Salih Ayyub's fractious succession struggles among Ayyubid princes.

relations.note: Kyiv destroyed December 1240; Rus principalities annihilated or subjugated
Mohi (April 1241): the Hungarian royal army destroyed
Legnica (April 1241): a Polish-German force crushed the same week as Mohi
Frederick II's total war with Pope Gregory IX
Valencia falls to James I (1238)
Nasrid Granada accepts Castilian tributary status at its founding (1238)

slices.label: Byzantium reborn, the Mongol world settles
events: Michael VIII Palaiologos retakes Constantinople; the Latin Empire ends after 57 years
The Golden Horde consolidates Mongol rule over the steppe and the tributary Rus principalities
Mamluks smash the Mongols at Ain Jalut (1260) and inherit Ayyubid Syria; Baghdad's Caliphate lies destroyed (1258)
slices.connectivityNote: Pax Mongolica beginning to knit the steppe into one trade zone even as Byzantium's restoration and Mamluk order stabilize the eastern Mediterranean.

entities.name: Kingdom of England
entities.note: Baronial reform crisis building toward the Second Barons' War (1264-67).

entities.name: Kingdom of Castile
entities.note: Seville conquered (1248); Alfonso X 'the Wise' presides over a golden age of translation at Toledo.

entities.name: Emirate of Granada
entities.note: Nasrid emirate secure as Castile's wealthy tributary, the sole surviving al-Andalus.

entities.name: Almohad Caliphate
entities.note: Reduced to Marrakesh and the High Atlas; Marinid tribesmen hold the north.

entities.name: Marinid Sultanate
entities.note: Zenata Berber dynasty holds Fez and the north, closing in on the last Almohads.

entities.name: County of Toulouse
entities.note: Awaiting reversion to the French crown on Alphonse of Poitiers's death (1271).

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Louis IX's Provence (via brother Charles of Anjou, count since 1246) points toward Mediterranean ambitions.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: The Great Interregnum (1250-73): no effective emperor since Frederick II's death (1250).

entities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
entities.note: Ottokar II expanding into Austria and the Alps.

entities.name: County of Flanders
entities.note: Peak cloth-town prosperity; Bruges rivals Paris.

entities.name: Republic of Genoa
entities.note: Treaty of Nymphaeum (1261) grants Genoa Black Sea trade privileges from restored Byzantium.

entities.name: Hohenstaufen Kingdom of Sicily
entities.note: Manfred, Frederick II's illegitimate son, rules a kingdom the Papacy is arming Charles of Anjou to conquer.

entities.name: Novgorod Republic
entities.note: Alexander Nevsky balances Mongol tribute against Swedish and German crusader pressure.

entities.name: Teutonic Order
entities.note: Great Prussian Uprising (1260-74) tests the Order's grip.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
entities.note: Mindaugas crowned king (1253) then reverts to paganism; state-building continues under pressure.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland
entities.note: Still fragmented among Piast duchies, rebuilding after Legnica.

entities.name: Rus Principalities
entities.note: Vladimir-Suzdal, Galicia-Volhynia, and Polotsk survive as Mongol tributaries under their own Rurikid princes.

entities.name: Golden Horde
entities.note: Berke Khan formally establishes the Golden Horde, converts to Islam, and rules the steppe and southern Rus.

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
entities.note: Béla IV rebuilds with stone castles after the Mongol catastrophe.

entities.name: Republic of Venice
entities.note: Loses its privileged Constantinople position to Genoa after 1261's Treaty of Nymphaeum.

entities.name: Kingdom of Serbia
entities.note: Uroš I expanding toward the Adriatic.

entities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire
entities.note: Reduced to its Danubian core after losing Macedonia and Thrace back to Byzantium.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: Michael VIII restores the Empire at Constantinople, but resources are stretched defending Europe and Asia at once.

entities.name: Principality of Achaea
entities.note: Defeated at Pelagonia (1259); cedes Mystras, Monemvasia and Maina to Byzantium (1262).

entities.name: Sultanate of Rum
entities.note: A Mongol vassal since Köse Dağ (1243); real power lies with the Mongol-backed vizier.

entities.name: Ilkhanate

entities.name: Kingdom of Cilician Armenia
entities.note: King Hetum I allies closely with the Mongols against the Mamluks.

entities.name: Kingdom of Georgia
entities.note: Mongol tributary kingdom, increasingly divided between rival royal lines.

entities.name: Mamluk Sultanate
entities.note: Baybars builds a formidable slave-soldier state after halting the Mongols at Ain Jalut (1260).

entities.name: Kingdom of Jerusalem (Acre)
entities.note: Kingdom of Jerusalem reduced to Acre and a shrinking coastal strip, squeezed by the Mamluks.

entities.name: Hafsid Ifriqiya
entities.note: Al-Mustansir briefly claims the caliphal title.

relations.note: Michael VIII favors Genoa, humiliating Venice's Levantine trade position

Ain Jalut (1260) halts the Mongol advance at the gates of Egypt
Berke Khan and Hulagu's rival Mongol houses fight over the Caucasus
Rurikid princes collect and remit the Mongol tribute (yarlyk system)
Great Interregnum leaves the Papacy free to arm Charles of Anjou against Hohenstaufen Sicily

slices.label: Acre falls, the Swiss rise, Edward I conquers Wales

Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swear the Rütli oath, founding the Swiss Confederacy
Sicilian Vespers (1282) leaves Aragonese Sicily facing Angevin Naples across the Straits of Messina; Edward I's conquest of Wales (1283) complete
slices.connectivityNote: Pax Mongolica lets Marco Polo-style caravans cross Eurasia in relative safety; Genoese and Venetian galleys dominate a reopened Mediterranean.

entities.name: Kingdom of England

entities.name: Kingdom of Scotland
entities.note: The 'Great Cause': the Maid of Norway dead (1290), rival claimants ask Edward I of England to arbitrate.

entities.name: Kingdom of Castile
entities.note: Sancho IV's succession disputes simmering ahead of the 'War of the Bands'.

entities.name: Kingdom of Navarre
entities.note: United with France's Capetian crown by marriage since 1284.

entities.name: Crown of Aragon
entities.note: Holding Sicily against a Papal-Angevin-French crusade launched over the Vespers.

entities.name: Marinid Sultanate

entities.name: Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen
entities.note: Squeezed between Marinid and Hafsid ambitions.

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Philip IV inherits Europe's richest, most centralized kingdom; Toulouse fully absorbed since 1271.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire

entities.name: Swiss Confederacy

entities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
entities.note: Ottokar II slain at Marchfeld (1278); Wenceslas II rebuilding.

entities.name: County of Flanders
entities.note: Guy of Dampierre chafes under French royal overlordship.

entities.name: Republic of Genoa
entities.note: Dominates Black Sea trade after Nymphaeum; crushes Pisa at Meloria (1284).

entities.name: Papal States

entities.name: Angevin Kingdom of Naples

entities.name: Aragonese Kingdom of Sicily

entities.name: Republic of Pisa
entities.note: Crushed at the naval Battle of Meloria (1284); Sardinia and Corsica now contested with Genoa.

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark
entities.note: Eric V assassinated (1286); baronial unrest.

entities.name: Kingdom of Norway
entities.note: Succession crisis after the death of the Maid of Norway (1290).

entities.name: Finnic Tribes
entities.note: Northern Finland and Sápmi remain outside state control.

entities.name: Teutonic Order

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
entities.note: Traidenis and successors resist both the Teutonic Order and the Golden Horde.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland
entities.note: Still fragmented; Přemysl II briefly crowned king (1295, just after this slice).

entities.name: Rus Principalities
entities.note: Vladimir-Suzdal, Galicia-Volhynia, and Polotsk persist as Mongol tributaries.

entities.name: Golden Horde

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
entities.note: Last Árpád kings weakened by the rise of the 'oligarch' magnates.

entities.name: Republic of Venice

entities.name: Kingdom of Serbia

entities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire
entities.note: Tatar (Golden Horde) overlordship and internal boyar strife.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire

entities.name: Despotate of Epirus

entities.name: Principality of Achaea

entities.name: Sultanate of Rum

entities.name: Ilkhanate

entities.name: Kingdom of Cilician Armenia

entities.name: Lusignan Kingdom of Cyprus

entities.name: Kingdom of Georgia
entities.note: Mongol tributary kingdom drifting toward internal fragmentation.

entities.name: Mamluk Sultanate

entities.note: Peace of Caltabellotta (1302, just ahead) will confirm Aragonese Sicily.

entities.name: Marinid Sultanate

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire

entities.name: Aragonese Kingdom of Sicily

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark

War of the Sicilian Vespers grinds on toward the 1302 Peace of Caltabellotta

slices.label: Valois France, an independent Scotland, a Byzantium at war with itself

Scotland's independence recognized by England at Edinburgh-Northampton (1328) after Bannockburn (1314)
Byzantium emerges from a ruinous civil war (1321-28) fatally weakened; Ottomans take Bursa as their capital (1326)
slices.connectivityNote: Trade still near its medieval peak, though Byzantine collapse in Anatolia and Mongol khanate rivalries begin to fray the eastern routes.

entities.name: Kingdom of England
entities.note: Edward III still a minor; Mortimer and Isabella rule, humiliated by Scotland's recognized independence.

entities.name: Kingdom of Scotland
entities.note: Full independence recognized by the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton (1328) after Bruce's victory at Bannockburn (1314).

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Philip VI's Valois succession is disputed by Edward III of England, his closest Capetian cousin.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Louis IV of Bavaria at odds with the Avignon Papacy.

entities.name: Swiss Confederacy
entities.note: Victory at Morgarten (1315) over Habsburg forces cements the Confederacy.

entities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
entities.note: John of Luxembourg, the 'blind king', adds Silesia's Piast duchies as vassals (1327).

entities.name: County of Flanders
entities.note: Flemish urban militias crushed at Cassel (1328) by the French crown.

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: Papacy resident at Avignon (since 1309) under French influence; Rome itself neglected.

entities.name: Angevin Kingdom of Naples
entities.note: Robert the Wise presides over Europe's leading Guelph power.

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark
entities.note: Christopher II's crown mortgaged to Holstein counts; near state collapse.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
entities.note: Gediminas expanding into Rus lands; founds Vilnius as capital.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland

entities.name: Rus Principalities

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Muscovy

entities.name: Golden Horde

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
entities.note: Charles I Robert of Anjou breaks the 'oligarch' magnates and opens gold mines at Kremnica.

entities.name: Kingdom of Serbia
entities.note: Stefan Dečanski crushes Bulgaria at Velbazhd (1330, imminent), cementing Serbian primacy in the Balkans.

entities.name: Byzantine Empire
entities.note: Just emerged from a ruinous civil war between Andronikos II and III (1321-28); the state is hollowed out.

entities.name: Knights Hospitaller (Rhodes)
entities.note: Holds Rhodes since 1310, a fortified Christian outpost astride Aegean-Levant shipping lanes.

entities.name: Duchy of Athens
entities.note: Under Catalan Company rule since their 1311 conquest at the Battle of Halmyros.

entities.name: Ottoman Beylik/Sultanate

entities.name: Kingdom of England

entities.name: Marinid Sultanate
entities.note: Overreach in Iberia (defeat at Río Salado, 1340) checks further expansion.

entities.name: Kingdom of France
entities.note: Flower of French chivalry destroyed at Crécy; Philip VI's authority shaken.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire
entities.note: Charles IV of Luxembourg-Bohemia elected king of the Romans.

entities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia

entities.name: County of Flanders

entities.name: Republic of Genoa

entities.name: Papal States
entities.note: Avignon Papacy; Cola di Rienzo's Roman republic agitation brewing.

entities.name: Angevin Kingdom of Naples
entities.note: Queen Joanna I's troubled succession after Robert the Wise's death (1343).

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark
entities.note: Valdemar IV begins reclaiming pawned crown lands.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
entities.note: Algirdas and Kęstutis co-rule a rapidly expanding pagan state pushing deep into Rus lands.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland
entities.note: Casimir III 'the Great' building royal castles and codifying law; Galicia-Volhynia conquest imminent (1349).

entities.name: Rus Principalities

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Muscovy

entities.name: Golden Horde

entities.name: Voivodeship of Wallachia

entities.name: Voivodeship of Moldavia

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary

entities.name: Kingdom of Serbia

entities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire

entities.name: Empire of Trebizond

entities.name: Kingdom of Cilician Armenia

entities.name: Kingdom of Castile

entities.name: Crown of Aragon

entities.name: Republic of Genoa

entities.name: Angevin Kingdom of Naples

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark

entities.name: Kingdom of Norway

uncertainties: Region AND (Andalusia) is mapped to Granada (granada) from 1241 onward rather than Castile, because the tessellation has no separate code for Christian-conquered Seville/Córdoba vs the Nasrid emirate; the larger Castilian-held western Andalusia is thus folded into Castile's CAS_S/CAS_N codes as a simplification.

Region VOL (Volhynia & Galicia/Lviv) genuinely split between Poland (Galicia, from Casimir III 1349) and Lithuania (Volhynia, from Liubartas ~1340s) for most of the era; assigned to Lithuania from 1360 onward per the era brief's explicit instruction that Lithuania holds BLR/UKR_W/VOL by 1396, with Poland's Galician claim logged here.

Epirus Despotate's post-1261 continuity is compressed: shown briefly folded into restored Byzantium at 1261, then shown independent again from 1291 - the real 1260s-80s situation involved rapid changes of ruling family (Doukas, then Orsini) not separately tracked.

Introduced non-canonical but historically standard entity ids for polities not in the registry: al_andalus (post-Almohad Taifa, 1228-1238), toulouse, flanders, burgundy_valois, karaman, anatolian_beyliks, jalayirid, aq_qoyunlu (unused after all, timurid covers the final slice), timurid, achaea, athens_duchy, hospitallers, cyprus_lusignan, zayyanid.

Aegean islands (AEG, Duchy of the Archipelago/Naxos under the Sanudo family) and Dalmatia (DAL) are folded into 'venice' throughout as Venetian-vassal/dependent territories rather than tracked as separate micro-states.

Denmark, Norway and Sweden are kept as three separate entities through 1396 even though Margaret I ruled all three in practice from 1389 (Sweden) — the formal Kalmar Union treaty falls in 1397, one year after the final slice, so the three-crown merge is deferred to era10.

Population figures for 1204-1300 are interpolated upward toward the ~75-80M European peak c.1300-1340 (McEvedy & Jones/HYDE-style estimates); the 1346->1360 slice applies a 35-50% cut per entity to reflect Black Death mortality, heavier in trade-exposed/urbanized polities (Genoa, Florence-adjacent Tuscany, Norway) and lighter in less-exposed interior polities (Bohemia, Teutonic Prussia) per the historiographical consensus on regional variation.

Golden Horde / Ilkhanate / Jalayirid / Timurid population figures include large off-map (Central Asian/Iranian) populations; only the in-map (Pontic steppe, Caucasus, Mesopotamia) share is intended to be read literally, per extendsBeyondMap:true.

Wallachia and Moldavia founding dates follow the data-spec's canonical years (1330, 1346) even though Moldavia's full independence under Bogdan I is more precisely dated 1359; both are used consistently with the spec's registry.
Cilician Armenia's fall is treated as complete by the 1380 slice (Mamluk conquest, 1375) rather than tracking the brief final Lusignan claimant period.

Bosnia and pre-1204 Toulouse are given informal founding dates (1154, 850) not specified in the canonical registry, chosen from standard reference dates for Ban Kulin and the Carolingian-era county respectively.
